extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students studying differential geometry, manifolds, and Riemann surfaces
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and worked examples about smooth/topological manifolds, differential forms on manifolds, orientability, Stokes' theorem, tangent/cotangent spaces, and basic Riemann surface theory. Includes exercises and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between vector fields and 1-forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a vector field F with the differential 1-form α = F1 e^1 + F2 e^2 + F3 e^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exterior-derivative computations (dα) and Hodge star to recover familiar vector calculus operators (e.g., dα corresponds to curl; taking the Hodge star and dropping the ∨’s gives ∇×F). This completes the correspondence between the 18.02 notation and the Napkin notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divergence definition (on R^3)
rubrics_metrics.description: div(F) := ∇·F := ∂F1/∂x + ∂F2/∂y + ∂F3/∂z, which is a scalar-valued function for input points p ∈ R^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scalar-valued divergence coincides with evaluation at the 3-form dα when α is the 2-form corresponding to F (see Problem 45C). The ∇· notation can be (informally) thought of as a dot product of ∇ = ⟨∂/∂x, ∂/∂y, ∂/∂z⟩ and F = ⟨F1,F2,F3⟩.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double derivative property (d^2 = 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exterior derivative satisfies d^2 = 0; composing two d arrows gives zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In vector-calculus terms: the curl of a gradient is zero, and the flux of a curl is zero — these are instances of the same theorem coming from d^2 = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stokes' theorem (cell / classical instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stokes' theorem for cells yields classical vector-calculus theorems as special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances: the three arrows from 0-D to 1-D are the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (or FTC for line integrals for n>1); for n=2 the other red arrow gives Green's theorem; for n=3 the arrow from work to flux is the (confusingly named) Stokes' theorem for surfaces; the rightmost arrow for n=3 is the divergence theorem. Each is an instance of the general Stokes framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green's theorem (formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For smooth functions f,g : R^2 → R and c a 2-cell, ∫_c (∂g/∂x − ∂f/∂y) dx∧dy = ∫_{∂c} (f dx + g dy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as Problem 45A to be worked out; it is the n=2 case of Stokes' theorem (cells).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback commutes with exterior derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: For open sets U,U' in vector spaces V,V' and smooth map ϕ:U→U', for any differential form α on U' we have ϕ^*(dα) = d(ϕ^*α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem 45D: proves naturality of d with respect to pullback; essential compatibility condition when transporting forms between charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc length is not a 1-form
rubrics_metrics.description: There does not exist a 1-form α on R^2 such that for every curve c:[0,1]→R^2 the integral ∫_c α gives the arc length of c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem 45E: shows arc length cannot be represented as the line integral of a globally defined 1-form on R^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact forms integrate equally on homologous cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: If α is an exact k-form (α = dβ for some β), then integrals of α over homologous cycles are equal; example: for exact 1-form α and any two concentric circles C1,C2 in the plane, ∫_{C1} α = ∫_{C2} α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem 45F: demonstrates that exactness implies path-independence on homologically trivial deformations (here concentric circles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological n-manifold definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological n-manifold M is a Hausdorff space with an open cover {Ui} such that each Ui is homeomorphic (by charts ϕi) to an open subset Ei ⊆ R^n; these charts form an atlas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two equivalent viewpoints: 'locally' every point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open set in R^n; 'globally' there exists an open cover by chart domains. The set of charts is called an atlas; charts and atlases enable intrinsic descriptions without embedding into R^N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth manifold definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth manifold is a topological manifold whose transition maps ϕ_ij (between overlapping chart images in R^n) are smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures compatibility of smooth structures induced from different charts. The same topological manifold can admit different smooth structures; smoothness is imposed by requiring smooth transition functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth map between manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f:M→R is smooth if composition with each chart ϕi (f∘ϕ_i^{-1}:Ei→R) is smooth. For f:M→N, f is smooth if for each chart pair the composed chart expression ϕ_j∘f∘ϕ_i^{-1}:Ei→Ej is smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smoothness is checked in local coordinates. This is the standard piecing-together definition: a map between manifolds is smooth iff it is smooth in every pair of compatible charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular value theorem (criterion for level sets to be manifolds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V be n-dimensional, U⊆V open, and f1,...,fm:U→R smooth. Let M = {p∈U | f1(p)=...=fm(p)=0}. If for each p∈M the linear map v↦((Df1)_p(v),...,(Dfm)_p(v)) has rank m, then M is a manifold of dimension n−m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary for m=1: if (Df)_p is nonzero on the zero set, the level set is a hypersurface of codimension 1. This is the standard criterion to construct manifolds as regular level sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential k-form on a manifold (compatibility condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A differential k-form α on a smooth manifold M is a collection {α_i} of differential k-forms on each chart image Ei such that for any overlap α_j = ϕ^*_{ij}(α_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other words, specify forms chartwise and require compatibility under pullbacks of transition maps so the local descriptions patch to a global form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientability (volume form criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth n-manifold is orientable if there exists a differential n-form ω on M such that ω_p ≠ 0 for every p∈M; such an ω is called a volume form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: an orientable manifold admits a consistent choice of sign for bases of tangent spaces. For embedded manifolds, orientability corresponds to a continuous nonzero normal vector field (e.g., S^1, S^2 orientable; Möbius strip and Klein bottle are not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and compactly supported forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The support of a differential form α on M is the closure of {p∈M | α_p ≠ 0}. If this support is compact, we say α is compactly supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume forms are typically supported on all of M. Compact support is the usual technical condition used in the statement of Stokes' theorem for manifolds in this text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stokes' theorem for manifolds (general statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a smooth oriented n-manifold with boundary and α is a compactly supported (n−1)-form, then ∫_M dα = ∫_{∂M} α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general manifold version of all the classical calculus theorems (FTC, Green's theorem, divergence theorem, etc.). The text omits some integration details and refers to [Sj05] for full development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent vector as derivation (intrinsic definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A derivation D at p is a linear map D:C^∞(M)→R satisfying the Leibniz rule D(fg)=f(p)D(g)+g(p)D(f). A tangent vector at p is a derivation; the tangent space T_p(M) is the set of all such derivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an intrinsic, embedding-free definition of tangent vectors: they act as directional-derivative-like linear maps on smooth functions. Equivalent formulations exist (see cotangent space construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotangent space via maximal ideal quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: Let m_p = {f∈C^∞(M) | f(p)=0} and m_p^2 = span{f_i g_i | f_i(p)=g_i(p)=0}. Then m_p/m_p^2 is the cotangent space (dual to the tangent space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, a tangent vector is a linear map m_p/m_p^2 → R. This algebraic definition is coordinate-free and useful in algebraic geometry contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension sanity check for tangent/cotangent spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For M⊆R^n open with 0∈M, m_0 = {smooth f | f(0)=0} and m_0^2 = {smooth f | f(0)=0,(∇f)_0=0}; thus m_0/m_0^2 ≅ R^n by mapping f ↦ (∂f/∂x1(0),...,∂f/∂xn(0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows the cotangent (and hence tangent) space has dimension n, matching classical expectations for manifolds modeled on R^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riemann surface definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Riemann surface X is a second countable connected Hausdorff space with an open cover {Ui} homeomorphic to open subsets Ei⊆C by charts ϕi, such that transition maps ϕ_ij are analytic functions. Each ϕi is a complex chart; together they form a complex atlas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: a (real) smooth 2-manifold endowed with a complex-analytic structure. In practice one often specifies finitely many complex charts rather than a maximal atlas. Local coordinates z=ϕ(x) are used; centered coordinates satisfy ϕ(p)=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex n-manifold definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A complex n-manifold is a Hausdorff space with an open cover by sets homeomorphic to open subsets of C^n, with analytic transition maps between chart images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complex n-manifold is naturally a smooth (real) 2n-manifold. The analytic (holomorphic) transition maps give the manifold its complex structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and non-examples of Riemann surfaces (criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open connected subsets of C and the Riemann sphere C_∞ (with stereographic charts whose transition map is z↦1/z) are Riemann surfaces; complex tori C/L with lattice L inherit complex structure from quotient; disjoint unions that are not connected are not Riemann surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct charts and verify analytic transitions (e.g., stereographic projection charts on S^2, quotient charts for C/L where transitions are translations). Connectivity is required in the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms between Riemann surfaces (holomorphic maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f:X→Y between Riemann surfaces is a morphism iff it is holomorphic at every point: in charts ϕ1 on X and ϕ2 on Y the composition ϕ2∘f∘ϕ1^{-1} is holomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holomorphicity is checked in local complex coordinates. Examples: polynomial maps C→C (e.g., z↦z^3) and the inclusion C→C_∞ are morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meromorphic functions as holomorphic maps to the Riemann sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Any meromorphic function f:X→C corresponds to a holomorphic map g:X→C_∞ defined by g(z)=f(z) when f(z)≠∞ and g(z)=∞ when f(z)=∞. Conversely, holomorphic maps to C_∞ not identically ∞ correspond to meromorphic functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poles of f become points mapped to ∞ on the Riemann sphere; reparametrizing near ∞ (t=1/z) shows analyticity at those points. Proposition: one-to-one correspondence between meromorphic functions X→C and holomorphic maps X→C_∞ not identically ∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a nonconstant holomorphic map between compact Riemann surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are compact and f:X→Y is holomorphic and nonconstant, then for each y∈Y the total multiplicity d_y of points in f^{-1}(y) is well-defined and constant; this common value is deg(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local analysis: near each point f is either a local isomorphism or locally of the form z↦z^k. Example: z↦z^k extended as a map C_∞→C_∞ has degree k. This constancy fails for arbitrary smooth compact manifolds but holds in the holomorphic/complex setting.
